hints: Look carefully at the word mitosis. Does it mean the whole cell cycle, or just the division of the nucleus?
Recall the four stages that start with P, M, A, T. Which of 1, 2 and 3 fits that list, and which happen before or after nuclear division?
walkthrough:
**Remember what mitosis really is**

Mitosis means nuclear division only. It is just one small part of the much larger cell cycle. Think nucleus first, cytoplasm later.

**Test each event in turn**

1 interphase is the long growth phase before division, when DNA replicates. It is part of the cell cycle, not part of mitosis.

2 telophase is the last of the four mitotic stages after prophase, metaphase and anaphase. The two new nuclei reform here, so this IS mitosis.

3 cytokinesis is division of the cytoplasm to make two separate cells. It usually follows mitosis, but it is not nuclear division so it is not mitosis.

**Choose the matching combination**

Only 2 is part of mitosis. That gives 2 only, which is option D.

options.A: Includes interphase and cytokinesis, which are parts of the cell cycle but not nuclear division, so this is too broad.
options.B: Both interphase (before division) and cytokinesis (cytoplasm division) are outside mitosis, so this combination is incorrect.
options.C: Telophase is correct, but cytokinesis is division of cytoplasm after the nuclei have formed, not part of mitosis.
options.D: Telophase is one of the four stages of mitosis, while 1 and 3 are not, so 2 only is correct.
